unit.title: Fractions and Decimals
unit.about_unit: Builds intuitive and rigorous understanding of fractions as equal parts of wholes and collections, equivalent fractions, and fraction strip models.

facilitation_guide.headline: Equal Sharing
facilitation_guide.text: Emphasize that parts must be strictly equal in area or quantity.

facilitation_guide.headline: Fraction Strips
facilitation_guide.text: Use tactile folding of paper strips to discover equivalent fractions visually.

chapter.title: Fractions
chapter.tagline: Discovering equal parts, fraction strips, and equivalent fractions through real-world sharing
chapter.overview: Tamanna has two chocolate bars of different sizes and discovers that one-third of a large bar is not the same as one-third of a small bar. Through fraction strips, rotis, and paper folding, students master equal sharing, fractions as numbers, and equivalent fractions.

sections.title: Tamanna's Chocolates: Equal Sharing of Unequal Wholes
sections.subtitle: Why the whole matters when comparing fractions

storyNarrative.dialogue: Kabir, I took 1/3 of my chocolate and you took 1/3 of yours, but my piece is much bigger! How can two 1/3 fractions have different amounts?

concept.heading: Fraction Relative to the Whole
concept.keyRule: A fraction represents a part of a specific whole; 1/3 of a 300g bar (100g) is greater than 1/3 of a 150g bar (50g).

sections.title: The Fraction Strips Wall
sections.subtitle: Visualizing halves, thirds, fourths, sixths, and eighths

storyNarrative.dialogue: When we align strips of equal length divided into 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 parts, we can immediately see which fraction is larger!

concept.heading: Unit Fractions & Strip Comparisons
concept.keyRule: For unit fractions with numerator 1, as the denominator increases, the size of each equal piece decreases (1/2 > 1/3 > 1/4 > 1/8).

sections.title: Equivalent Fractions: Same Value, Different Names
sections.subtitle: Discovering 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 = 4/8 with area models

storyNarrative.dialogue: Look at this circle: shading 1 out of 2 halves covers the exact same area as shading 2 out of 4 quarters!

concept.heading: Generating Equivalent Fractions
concept.keyRule: Multiplying or dividing both numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number produces an equivalent fraction (1/2 × 2/2 = 2/4).

sections.subtitle: Calculating fractions of quantities (e.g. 1/4 of 24 apples)

storyNarrative.dialogue: We have 24 apples in our basket. If we give 1/4 of them to our neighbors, how many apples is that?

concept.heading: Fraction as an Operator
concept.keyRule: To find 1/n of a quantity Q, divide Q by n. To find m/n of Q, divide Q by n and multiply by m.
